extracted.intended_audience: sellers, telemarketers, compliance officers, and attorneys responsible for Telemarketing Sales Rule (16 CFR Part 310) compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and prohibitions under the Federal Trade Commission's Telemarketing Sales Rule (16 CFR Part 310) governing deceptive and abusive telemarketing practices, recordkeeping, exemptions, Do-Not-Call access fees, and enforcement notice procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material information before consent to pay (§310.3(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a customer consents to pay for goods or services offered, the seller or telemarketer must truthfully disclose, in a clear and conspicuous manner, material information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material information that must be disclosed includes: (i) total costs to purchase/receive/use and quantity of goods/services; (ii) all material restrictions, limitations, or conditions to purchase/receive/use; (iii) seller's refund/cancellation/exchange/repurchase policy or all material terms if representations are made; (iv) in prize promotions, odds of receiving the prize (or factors used to calculate odds), that no purchase is required, and the no-purchase/no-payment method with instructions or contact info; (v) all material costs/conditions to receive/redeem a prize; (vi) limits on cardholder liability for unauthorized credit card use (15 U.S.C. 1643) when relevant; (vii) if a negative option feature is included, all material terms of that feature including that charges will occur unless customer takes affirmative action, dates of charge submission, and steps to avoid charges; and (viii) in the sale of any debt relief service, detailed disclosures about time to results, settlement-offer timing and amounts, adverse effects on creditworthiness, and customer rights regarding funds in accounts (with cross-references to §310.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misrepresentations in sales (§310.3(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is prohibited to misrepresent, directly or by implication, material information in the sale of goods or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of prohibited misrepresentations include: total costs or quantities; material restrictions/limitations; material aspects of performance, efficacy, nature, or central characteristics; material aspects of refund/cancellation/exchange/repurchase policies; prize promotion aspects (odds, nature/value, whether purchase is required); material aspects of investment opportunities (risk, liquidity, earnings potential); false affiliation/endorsement/sponsorship by any person or government entity; claims that offered goods/services provide protections a customer already has; material aspects of negative option features; and material aspects of any debt relief service (including money saved, time to results, credit effects, success rates, nonprofit status).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express verifiable authorization required before charging billing information (§310.3(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A seller or telemarketer may not cause billing information to be submitted for payment, or collect/attempt payment, without the customer's or donor's express verifiable authorization (with limited exceptions for certain credit/debit cards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization is deemed verifiable if one of the following is used: (i) express written authorization including the customer's signature (electronic signatures count where legally recognized); (ii) express oral authorization that is audio-recorded and made available upon request and that clearly evidences both the customer's authorization and receipt of specified information (accurate description; number of debits/charges; dates charges will be submitted; amounts; customer's name; billing information identified with sufficient specificity; a customer inquiry telephone number answered during normal business hours; date of oral authorization); or (iii) written confirmation sent via first class mail prior to submission identified on the outside as confirmation and containing the same specified information plus a clear statement of refund procedures; written-confirmation method is not verifiable for free-to-pay conversions using preacquired account information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on false or misleading statements to induce payment (§310.3(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a violation to make false or misleading statements to induce any person to pay for goods or services or to induce a charitable contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a standalone prohibition separate from the specific disclosure and misrepresentation provisions; any deceptive statement or implication intended to induce payment or donation is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assisting or facilitating violative telemarketing (§310.3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person violates the rule if they provide substantial assistance or support to any seller or telemarketer when that person knows or consciously avoids knowing that the seller or telemarketer is engaged in acts or practices that violate specified sections (§§ 310.3(a),(c),(d), or §310.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers third parties, vendors, and service providers who enable deceptive or abusive telemarketing when they have knowledge or deliberately avoid learning of wrongdoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on credit card laundering (§310.3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as expressly permitted by the applicable credit card system, it is deceptive and prohibited to present for payment, or cause to be presented for payment, a credit card sales draft generated by a telemarketing transaction that is not the result of a telemarketing credit card transaction between the cardholder and the merchant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also prohibits employing or causing a merchant (or its agents) to present such drafts and obtaining unauthorized access to the credit card system through business relationships or affiliations not authorized by the merchant agreement or the credit card system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited deceptive acts in solicitation of charitable contributions (§310.3(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Telemarketers soliciting charitable contributions must not misrepresent material information about the charity or the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically prohibits misrepresenting the entity's nature/purpose/mission; claiming tax deductibility when not true; misrepresenting the purpose for which contributions will be used; misrepresenting the percentage/amount of a contribution that will go to the organization or a particular program; misrepresenting prize promotion aspects (odds, nature/value, or that contribution is required to win); and misrepresenting affiliation/endorsement/sponsorship by any person or government entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on abusive conduct generally (§310.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an abusive telemarketing act or practice to engage in certain types of harassing, coercive, or otherwise abusive conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated abusive acts include: (1) threats, intimidation, or profane/obscene language; (2) requesting/receiving payment to remove/repair credit information before seller has delivered and provided consumer report evidence (with timing rules); (3) requesting/receiving payment to recover/return money or items from a prior transaction until seven business days after delivery (except licensed attorneys); (4) requesting/receiving payment in advance to obtain a loan when seller/telemarketer guarantees or represents a high likelihood of success; (5) restrictions on charging for debt relief services until specific renegotiation/settlement milestones are met and related rules about funds-accounts administration; (6) disclosing or receiving for consideration unencrypted consumer account numbers for use in telemarketing (with limited processing-payment exceptions); (7) causing billing information to be submitted without the customer's express informed consent (with detailed preacquired-account rules); (8) failing to transmit telephone number (and name where available) to caller ID services used by recipients (with permitted substitutions); (9) creating remotely created payment orders as payment for telemarketing transactions; and (10) accepting cash-to-cash money transfers or cash reload mechanisms as payment for telemarketing sales or charitable contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt relief payment timing and fee restrictions (§310.4(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific prohibitions and requirements govern when a seller/telemarketer may request or receive payment for debt relief services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A debt relief seller may not request or receive any fee until: (A) the seller has renegotiated/settled/reduced or otherwise altered the terms of at least one debt pursuant to a valid agreement executed by the customer; (B) the customer has made at least one payment under that agreement; and (C) fees must either (1) bear a proportional relationship to the part of the total debt renegotiated attributable to each individual debt, or (2) be a fixed percentage of the amount saved as a result of the renegotiation (the percentage cannot change between debts). Rules also permit customer-held accounts for fees and creditor payments only if stringent conditions are met (insured institution, customer owns funds, administrator is independent, no referral compensation, customer may withdraw without penalty and receive funds within seven business days, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preacquired account information — special consent and record rules (§310.4(a)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: When telemarketing uses preacquired account information (information enabling a charge to be placed without obtaining the number during the transaction), special consent and record requirements apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For preacquired account information combined with free-to-pay conversions: seller must obtain at minimum the last four digits of the account number, obtain express agreement to be charged using that account, and make and maintain an audio recording of the entire telemarketing transaction. For other transactions involving preacquired account information: seller must identify the account with sufficient specificity for the customer to understand which account will be charged and obtain express agreement to be charged using that account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caller identification transmission requirement (§310.4(a)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Telemarketers must transmit the telephone number and, when made available by the telemarketer's carrier, the name of the telemarketer to any caller identification service in use by a recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not a violation to substitute (for the name and phone number used in, or billed for, making the call) the name of the seller or charitable organization on whose behalf the telemarketing call is placed and the seller's/charitable organization's customer/donor service telephone number answered during regular business hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on creating remotely created payment orders (§310.4(a)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating or causing to be created a remotely created payment order as payment for goods/services or charitable contributions offered/sold through telemarketing is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule covers remotely created checks and other payment orders created by payee or its agent and cleared through the check clearing system, except payments cleared through ACH or subject to Truth in Lending Act/Regulation Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting certain cash-based payment mechanisms (§310.4(a)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting cash-to-cash money transfers or cash reload mechanisms as payment for telemarketing sales or telephonic charitable solicitations is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cash-to-cash money transfers and cash reload mechanisms are defined in §310.2 and include transfers where cash is sent and received as cash at a different location and mechanisms that convert cash to electronic forms used to add funds to general-use prepaid cards or intermediary accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern of calls / Do-Not-Call compliance (§310.4(b)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Telemarketers and sellers must not engage in abusive calling patterns and must comply with Do-Not-Call and individual do-not-call requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited conduct includes: (i) causing any telephone to ring or engaging any person repeatedly or continuously with intent to annoy/abuse/harass; (ii) denying or interfering with a person's right to be placed on any do-not-call registry or honoring such requests (including harassing, hanging up, failing to honor, requiring a sales pitch before accepting the request, charging a fee, requiring another call to submit request, or requiring the person to identify the seller); and (iii) initiating outbound calls to persons who have stated they do not wish to receive such calls or whose numbers are on the Commission's National Do-Not-Call Registry, unless the seller can demonstrate written express agreement (signed, showing authorization and telephone number) or an established business relationship and the person has not stated they do not wish to receive calls (with related exceptions in the rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandoned call prohibition and definition (§310.4(b)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: An outbound telephone call is 'abandoned' if a person answers and the telemarketer does not connect the call to a sales representative within two seconds of the person's completed greeting; abandoning outbound calls is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section prohibits placing calls that systematically result in consumers answering but not being connected to a live sales representative in the required time. (Text truncated in source but the rule sets operational standards and exceptions elsewhere.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements — required records (§310.5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers and telemarketers must make and keep specific, complete, and accurate records documenting telemarketing activities and compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required records (illustrative listing as set forth in the rule) include: training materials and scripts used in telemarketing; copies of seller-telemarketer agreements/contracts; records of consumer authorizations and confirmations (written, oral recordings, written-mail confirmations) evidencing verifiable authorizations; records documenting compliance with required disclosures, refund/cancellation policies, and negative option terms; dialing logs and call detail (including time/duration to the closest second and numbers in specified formats); audio recordings where oral authorization occurred; consumer complaint files and actions taken; records of do-not-call requests (name, telephone numbers, seller/charitable org, telemarketer, date of request, goods/services or charitable purpose); records of each service provider used to deliver outbound calls (contract, date signed, time period) retained for 5 years after contract expiration; and a record of which version of the Commission's Do-Not-Call registry was used to ensure compliance (entity name, date accessed, subscription account number, telemarketing campaign).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record format, timekeeping, retention and standards (§310.5(b)-(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Records may be kept in ordinary course of business formats but must meet specific formatting and timekeeping standards where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic telephone numbers must conform with the North American Numbering Plan; international numbers must conform to ITU-T E.164 standard; time and duration of calls must be kept to the closest second; time must be recorded in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Certain records (e.g., service provider contracts) must be kept for specified periods (for example, 5 years). Materials incorporated by reference (e.g., ITU standard) are available at FTC/NARA. Failure to keep records as required is a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping defenses and obligations on allocation (§310.5(d)-(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A seller/telemarketer may avoid liability for incomplete/inaccurate records if they can demonstrate routine business practices ensuring completeness and accuracy; parties may allocate recordkeeping responsibilities by written agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defensive documentation must show: (1) procedures to ensure record completeness/accuracy; (2) personnel training in those procedures; (3) monitoring and enforcement of procedures with records documenting that monitoring; and (4) any record failures were temporary, inadvertent, and corrected within 30 days of discovery. Written agreements allocating recordkeeping responsibility are permitted; if allocated to the telemarketer, the seller must implement practices to ensure compliance and retain access to records. On dissolution or change in ownership, principals or successors must maintain required records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from the rule (§310.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of calls/transactions are exempt from some or all requirements of this part, subject to conditions and enumerated exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions include: (1) solicitations to induce charitable contributions via outbound calls are not covered by a particular cross-referenced requirement; (2) sale of pay-per-call services (16 CFR part 308) — but exemptions do not apply to some abusive provisions (§310.4(a)(1),(a)(8), (b), (c)); (3) sale of franchises/business opportunities subject to other FTC rules (with similar carve-outs); (4) telephone calls where sale/donation is completed only after a face-to-face presentation (with carve-outs); (5) telephone calls initiated by a customer or donor (with exceptions for upselling and certain products/services); (6) calls in response to advertisements (excluding certain categories like investment/debt relief/technical support/business opportunities and excluding upsells and some payment-method rules); (7) calls in response to direct mail that truthfully and conspicuously disclosed all material info (with exceptions); and (8) business-to-business calls (with exceptions and limited applicability to retailer sales of nondurable office/cleaning supplies). Each exemption contains specific exclusions where key prohibitions still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and private actions — FTC notice requirement (§310.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: State attorneys general or other authorized state officials and private persons bringing actions under the Telemarketing and Consumer Fraud and Abuse Prevention Act must serve written notice of their action on the Commission, if feasible, prior to initiating the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be sent to the Office of the Director, Bureau of Consumer Protection, FTC (tsrnotice@ftc.gov) and include a copy of the complaint and other pleadings. If prior notice is not feasible, notice must be served immediately upon instituting the action. The rule does not preclude state officials from proceeding in state court under state statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee and access rules for the National Do-Not-Call Registry (§310.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must pay an annual fee to access telephone numbers within an area code in the Commission's National Do-Not-Call Registry before initiating outbound calls to numbers in that area code (subject to exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual fee: $82 per area code accessed, up to a maximum ($22,626), with the first five area codes free. During the annual period there are fees for adding area codes ($82 for the first six months, $41 for the second six months). No cost-sharing arrangements are permitted to divide the cost among clients. Access is limited to telemarketers, sellers, service providers acting on their behalf, and government agencies with law enforcement authority. Persons accessing the registry must provide identifying information, pay fee, receive a unique account number, and certify under penalty of law that they will use the data only to comply with the rule or to prevent calls to numbers on the registry; agents accessing on behalf of sellers must identify each seller and provide each seller's unique account number and certify proper use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sharing cost or participation arrangements for registry access (§310.8(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: No person may participate in any arrangement to share the cost of accessing the National Do-Not-Call Registry so as to divide costs among various clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disallows cost-splitting arrangements between sellers, telemarketers, or service providers to circumvent the fee structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability (§310.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of Part 310 are separate and severable; if any provision is stayed or invalidated, the remaining provisions continue in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard severability clause indicating the Commission's intent that other provisions remain operative if one is found invalid.
